# Tela

> Tela is a desktop UI framework in pure Go (no cgo, no webview): React-style components and hooks, styled with Tailwind CSS v4 classes, drawn by its own renderer on Linux and Windows, and rendered headlessly to PNGs and aria snapshots so an agent can see what it built. This file is the whole guide an LLM needs to build good-looking Tela screens: the API, the `kit` components (shadcn/ui's look), the agent loop with `tela mcp`, a complete settings screen and the mistakes to avoid. Every Go block in it compiles against the current API.

Contents: 1 Start · 2 The agent loop · 3 Elements and props · 4 Components and hooks · 5 Styling · 6 kit · 7 A complete settings screen · 8 Windows and desktop services · 9 Pitfalls and limits · 10 Testing · More

## 1. Start

- Tela draws every pixel (like Flutter or a browser). There is no HTML, DOM, CSS file or JavaScript: a tree of Go values describes the UI.
- Elements and props come from package `h` (dot-imported, so markup reads like JSX); the app, hooks, events and colors from `tela`; ready-made styled components from `kit`.
- Components are struct values with a `Build() tela.Node` method, or functions wrapped in `tela.C`/`tela.CP`. Hooks (`tela.UseState`...) follow React's rules.
- Styling is `Class("...")` with Tailwind v4 class names, verbatim. Theme tokens (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`) follow light and dark.
- Go 1.27+, always `CGO_ENABLED=0`. Lucide icons are a separate module.

```sh
mkdir myapp && cd myapp && go mod init example.com/myapp
go get github.com/kuronosu/tela@latest github.com/kuronosu/tela/icons/lucide@latest
CGO_ENABLED=0 go install github.com/kuronosu/tela/cmd/tela@latest   # the CLI: tela mcp, snapshot, inspect, lint, dev
# or: tela new myapp  (a counter app with a test, go.mod ready)
go mod tidy   # after you add imports: kit and aria need golang.org/x/text
```

The imports of a screen:

```go
import (
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/kit"

	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/icons/lucide" // lucide.Check, lucide.Settings, ... (Lucide's file names in CamelCase)
)
```

The smallest complete app. `var App` is the window that `main` opens and the screen that `tela snapshot` and `tela mcp` render:

```go
package main

import (
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/kit"
)

// Counter is the public name; tela.C gives counter its own hook state.
func Counter() tela.Node { return tela.C(counter) }

func counter() tela.Node {
	count, setCount := tela.UseState(0)
	return Div(Class("flex min-h-screen items-center justify-center"),
		kit.Card{
			Class:       "w-72",
			Title:       Text("Counter"),
			Description: Textf("Clicked %d times", count),
			Footer: kit.Button{Class: "w-full", Children: Text("Add one"),
				OnClick: func() { setCount.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 }) }},
		})
}

var theme = kit.Theme() // shadcn/ui's neutral colors and 10 px radius: use it with kit

var App = tela.App{
	Title: "Counter", Width: 480, Height: 320,
	Theme: &theme, RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground",
	Root: Counter(),
}

func main() { tela.Main(App) }
```

**What the CLI and `tela mcp` mount** (the package may be `main` or any package):

- `var Previews = tela.Previews{...}`: several named screens; `--preview NAME` (or the `open` tool) picks one, else the first name in byte order. Wins over the others.
- `func Preview() tela.Node`: one screen, mounted as `tela.C(Preview)`, so it may call hooks itself. (`func Preview() tela.Component` is called and its result mounted.)
- Otherwise `var App = tela.App{...}`: its `Root` is the screen.
- In every case `var App` (a `tela.App` or `*tela.App`) gives the window: `Width`/`Height` (default 960x640), `RootClass`, `Theme`, `ColorScheme`, `ClassAliases`. Without `RootClass` the window is white with black text.

```go
// One screen; it may use hooks because it is mounted as tela.C(Preview).
func Preview() tela.Node {
	open, setOpen := tela.UseState(true)
	return Div(Class("p-8"), kit.Switch{Checked: &open, OnCheckedChange: setOpen.Set, AriaLabel: "Open"})
}

// Several screens, each started in the state its fields give it.
var Previews = tela.Previews{
	"1 Empty": {Root: Inbox{}},
	"2 Full":  {Root: Inbox{Unread: 12}},
}

type Inbox struct{ Unread int }

func (in Inbox) Build() tela.Node {
	return Div(Class("p-8 text-sm"), Textf("%d unread", in.Unread))
}
```

`tela.App` fields: `Title`, `AppID`, `Width`, `Height`, `RootClass`, `Root` (a `tela.Component`: `Settings()`, `Settings{}`, `kit.Toaster{Children: ...}`), `ColorScheme` (`tela.System`, the zero value, follows the OS; `tela.Light`, `tela.Dark`), `Theme *tela.Theme`, `ClassAliases`, `ClassicScrollbars`, `InstantScroll`, `Dev *bool`. `tela.Main(app)` opens the window and runs until it closes; `tela.Run(app)` returns the error instead.

## 2. The agent loop

Write the package, look at it, fix, repeat. `tela mcp` keeps a headless instance of the screen running and rebuilds it when the source changes.

```sh
claude mcp add tela -- tela mcp ./myapp          # Claude Code; other clients: {"command": "tela", "args": ["mcp", "./myapp"]}
tela mcp [--size WxH] [--scale N] [--dark] [--preview NAME] [pkg]
```

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `snapshot {}` | Aria snapshot (Playwright YAML) with `[ref=eN]` on what you can act on. Cheap: call it after every edit |
| `screenshot {}` / `{"ref": "e5"}` | PNG of the window or one element. Judge the look here: spacing, alignment, contrast, dark mode |
| `click {"ref": "e5"}` | Real pointer click; `"button": "right"`, `"double": true`, or `"x"`, `"y"` |
| `fill {"ref": "e7", "text": "ana@example.com"}` | Replace a text field's value; `"submit": true` presses Enter |
| `press {"key": "Tab"}` | Key or combo in Playwright syntax (`Enter`, `Shift+Tab`, `Control+a`, `ArrowDown`), optionally on a `ref` |
| `hover`, `scroll {"ref", "dy": 400}`, `drag {"from", "to" or "dx"/"dy"}` | Pointer moves, wheel, drags |
| `resize {"width": 390, "height": 844}` / `{"scale": 2}` | Keeps the state; breakpoints follow |
| `open {"dark": true}` / `{"preview": "2 Full"}` | Mount afresh (state reset) in dark mode, another preview, size or scale; `{}` lists the previews |
| `wait {"ms": 500}` / `{"text": "Saved"}` | Advance the app clock (timers, `UseTimeout`, animations, toasts) or wait for a text |
| `inspect {"ref": "e5"}` | Layout JSON: rects, margin/border/padding, classes, class errors, computed style. Use it when something is misplaced |
| `lint {}` | `tela lint -json` on the package |

Elements are named by `ref` (from the latest snapshot), or `role` + `name`, `text`, `testId`, with `nth`. Every acting tool returns the new snapshot.

**Reading a result.** The text has sections: `### Snapshot` (YAML), `### Dev errors` (unknown classes with "did you mean": fix these first), `### Dev warnings` (missing keys, nil dependencies), `### Lint`, `### Output of the app`. A dev-mode panic (an unknown role, a misused hook) is the error of the call, with the fix in its message, and the screen is mounted afresh. A first line "The source changed: rebuilt ... and mounted afresh (state reset)" means your edit is live. "The package does not compile:" is followed by the compiler's errors, and the previous build keeps answering. "The new build compiles, but its screen cannot be mounted" is a panic while mounting (often a hook misuse; the message names the fix).

**A good loop.** 1) Write the screen with `var App` (or `Preview`). 2) `snapshot`: fix every dev error and lint finding. 3) `screenshot`: fix the look. 4) `open {"dark": true}` + `screenshot`. 5) `click`/`fill` the main interactions and `screenshot` the states (open dialogs, toasts after `wait`). 6) `resize` to a narrow window if it must be responsive.

**CLI equivalents** (same rendering, deterministic, embedded fonts):

```sh
tela snapshot --size 1040x800 --scale 2 --dark -o out.png ./myapp   # PNG (W*scale x H*scale)
tela inspect ./myapp            # aria snapshot YAML; --layout for the layout JSON
tela lint ./...                 # unknown classes, roles, aria tokens, keys, hook misuse; file:line:col: rule: message
tela dev ./myapp                # a real window that reloads on save, keeping state
```

`tela snapshot` renders one frame: state set by effects, timers or toasts does not show in it; use `tela mcp` (`wait`) or a test for those.

## 3. Elements and props (`h`)

An element takes props and children in one list, in any order: `Div(Class("p-4"), H2(Text("Title")), OnClick(f))`. A string is not a child: `Div("x")` does not compile; write `Div(Text("x"))` or `Textf("%d items", n)`.

**Elements:** `Div` (block box; the general container), `Span` (inline in text; a flex item inside `flex`), `P`, `H1`..`H6` (unstyled, like Tailwind's Preflight: size them with classes; they give heading roles), `Button` (no look of its own, focusable, Enter/Space click), `A` (`Href`; does not navigate: handle `OnClick`), `Strong`, `Em`, `Code`, `Img` (`SrcPath`, `SrcFS`, `SrcBytes`, `Src(image.Image)`, `Alt`; PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG), `Icon(icon, props...)` (an SVG `tela.Icon`, 1em, colored by the text color), `Input`, `Textarea`, `Form` (`OnSubmit`; Enter submits), `Label` (`For`), `Text`, `Textf`, `TextFn(func() string)`, `Fragment(children...)` (no box), `Portal(children...)` (a layer above the window: overlays), `Presence(children...)` (keeps exiting children mounted), `VirtualList`. There is no `Ul`, `Li`, `Nav`, `Section`, `Header`, `Table` or `Select` element: use `Div` with `Role("list")`, `Role("navigation")`... and `kit` components.

**Props:** `Class(classes...)`, `Style(tela.Width(w), tela.Bg(c), ...)` (typed values computed in code; they win over classes), `Key(id)`, `ID`, `For`, `Disabled(bool)`, `TabIndex`, `AutoFocus`, `Ref(elementRef)`, `TestID`, `Dir("rtl")`, `Scheme(tela.Dark)` (a subtree in another color scheme), `Inert`, `Href`, `Alt`, `Tint(color)`; text fields: `Value`, `DefaultValue`, `Bind(text, setText)`, `BindValue(*tela.Value[string])`, `Placeholder`, `Type("email")`, `Rows`, `ReadOnly`, `MaxLength`, `Name`; accessibility: `Role("navigation")`, `AriaLabel`, `AriaLabelledBy(refs...)`, `AriaDescribedBy(ref)`, `AriaCurrent("page")` (`""` is none), `AriaChecked`, `AriaPressed`, `AriaExpanded`, `AriaSelected`, `AriaDisabled`, `AriaInvalid`, `AriaHidden`, `AriaSort`, `AriaHasPopup`, `AriaControls`, `AriaValueNow`, `AriaValueMin`, `AriaValueMax`, `AriaValueText` (live regions are `Role("status")` and `Role("alert")`); animation: `AnimateLayout()`, `LayoutID(id)`, `Exit(classes)`.

**Events:** `OnClick`, `OnDoubleClick`, `OnContextMenu`, `OnMouseDown/Up/Move/Enter/Leave`, `OnPointer...`, `OnLongPress`, `OnDrag`/`OnDragStart`/`OnDragEnd`, `OnWheel`, `OnScroll`, `OnKeyDown`/`OnKeyUp`, `OnFocus`/`OnBlur`, `OnChange` (every edit), `OnBeforeInput`, `OnSubmit`, `OnSelect`. Each takes a `func()` or a `func(e)` of its event type (`tela.MouseEvent`, `tela.KeyboardEvent`, `tela.ChangeEvent`...). Events bubble; `e.StopPropagation()`, `e.PreventDefault()`, or wrap a `func()` in `tela.StopPropagation(f)`.

**Helpers:** `If(cond, child)` and `IfElse(cond, a, b)` take and return a `tela.Child` (a node, a component or a prop); `Map(items, func(T) tela.Node)` and `MapIndex` (give each node a `Key`); `MapKeyed(items, keyFn, func(T) tela.Component)` keys components for you; `Range(n, render)` for static repeats (keyed by index); `Nodes([]tela.Node)` passes a slice built in a loop. Every argument of `If` is evaluated: `If(u != nil, Text(u.Name))` panics on nil `u`; use a Go `if`.

```go
type Todo struct {
	ID   int
	Text string
	Done bool
}

func TodoList(todos []Todo, remove func(id int)) tela.Node {
	return Div(Role("list"), AriaLabel("Todos"), Class("flex flex-col gap-2"),
		If(len(todos) == 0, P(Class("text-sm text-muted-foreground"), Text("Nothing to do."))),
		Map(todos, func(t Todo) tela.Node {
			return Div(Key(t.ID), Role("listitem"),
				Class("flex items-center justify-between rounded-md border border-border px-3 py-2"),
				Span(Class("text-sm"), If(t.Done, Class("text-muted-foreground line-through")), Text(t.Text)),
				Button(Class("text-sm text-destructive hover:underline"), AriaLabel("Remove "+t.Text),
					OnClick(func() { remove(t.ID) }), Text("Remove")))
		}))
}

func Shortcuts(save func()) tela.Node {
	return Div(TabIndex(0), Class("rounded-md p-4 outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"),
		OnKeyDown(func(e tela.KeyboardEvent) {
			if e.Ctrl && e.Key == "s" {
				e.PreventDefault()
				save()
			}
		}),
		Text("Press Ctrl+S to save"))
}
```

**Raw text fields** (prefer `kit.Input` and `kit.Field`, which are styled and wired):

```go
func Search() tela.Node {
	q, setQ := tela.UseState("")
	return Form(OnSubmit(func() { fmt.Println("search", q) }),
		Input(Type("search"), Placeholder("Search"), AriaLabel("Search"), Bind(q, setQ),
			Class("h-9 w-64 rounded-md border border-input bg-transparent px-3 text-sm placeholder:text-muted-foreground",
				"focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring/50")))
}
```

**Long lists:** `VirtualList(count, estimateSize, renderItem, props...)` builds only the visible rows; it is the scroll container (style it like a `Div`). `renderItem` returns a node or a component and must not call hooks (return a struct component for rows with state). `ItemKey(func(i int) K)` keys rows by identity.

```go
type Row struct{ Name string }

func (r Row) Build() tela.Node {
	return Div(Class("flex h-12 items-center border-b border-border px-4 text-sm"), Text(r.Name))
}

func People(names []string) tela.Node {
	return VirtualList(len(names), func(int) float32 { return 48 },
		func(i int) tela.Component { return Row{Name: names[i]} },
		ItemKey(func(i int) string { return names[i] }),
		Class("h-96 rounded-lg border border-border"))
}
```

## 4. Components and hooks

**Struct components** are the default: the fields are the props, `Build` has a value receiver, children are a field of type `tela.Component` (several via `Fragment(...)`). A struct value used as a child is its own component, with its own state, and its build is skipped while its fields are `==` to the previous ones (func or slice fields make it rebuild every time; that is fine).

```go
type Stat struct {
	Label, Value, Trend string
}

func (s Stat) Build() tela.Node {
	return Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-1 rounded-xl border border-border bg-card p-5 shadow-xs"),
		P(Class("text-sm text-muted-foreground"), Text(s.Label)),
		P(Class("text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight tabular-nums"), Text(s.Value)),
		P(Class("text-xs font-medium text-emerald-600 dark:text-emerald-400"), Text(s.Trend)))
}

type Section struct {
	Title    string
	Children tela.Component
}

func (s Section) Build() tela.Node {
	open, setOpen := tela.UseState(true)
	return Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-3"),
		Button(Class("text-left text-sm font-semibold"), OnClick(tela.Toggle(setOpen)), AriaExpanded(open), Text(s.Title)),
		If(open, s.Children))
}

// A struct component is a tela.Component, not a tela.Node: Fragment makes it one.
// Never call Section{...}.Build(): its hooks would run in the caller.
func Overview() tela.Node {
	return Fragment(Section{Title: "This week", Children: Div(Class("grid grid-cols-3 gap-4"),
		Stat{Label: "Revenue", Value: "$12,480", Trend: "+8.1%"},
		Stat{Label: "Orders", Value: "342", Trend: "+3.4%"},
		Stat{Label: "Refunds", Value: "4", Trend: "-1.2%"})})
}
```

**Function components** use `tela.C(fn)` (no props) or `tela.CP(fn, props)` (comparable props, skipped while `==`). Write the wrap once in a public function, so callers never call the private one:

```go
func Clock() tela.Node { return tela.C(clock) }

func clock() tela.Node {
	now, setNow := tela.UseState(time.Now())
	tela.UseInterval(time.Second, func() { setNow.Set(time.Now()) })
	return Span(Class("tabular-nums"), Text(now.Format("15:04:05")))
}

type BadgeProps struct{ Count int }

func Unread(p BadgeProps) tela.Node { return tela.CP(unread, p) }

func unread(p BadgeProps) tela.Node {
	return Span(Class("rounded-full bg-primary px-2 text-xs font-medium text-primary-foreground"), Textf("%d", p.Count))
}
```

Keys: an element takes `Key(id)`; a component or fragment is keyed with `tela.WithKey(Card{...}, id)` (which also turns it into a `tela.Node`), or `tela.C(fn, Key(id))`, `tela.CP(fn, p, Key(id))`, or `MapKeyed`.

**Hooks** (call them at the top of a component, same order every build, never in `if`/`for`/after an early `return`/inside callbacks or `Map` functions):

| Hook | Does |
|---|---|
| `v, set := tela.UseState(init)` | State; `set.Set(v)`, `set.Update(func(T) T)` (use `Update` when the new value depends on the old). `set` is a comparable `tela.Setter[T]`, safe from any goroutine; `tela.Toggle(set)` flips a bool |
| `s, d := tela.UseReducer(reduce, init)` | `d.Dispatch(action)`; reducer `func(S, A) S` |
| `tela.UseEffect(f, deps...)` | After the frame is presented; `f` returns a cleanup or nil. No deps: every build; `tela.Once`: mount only. `UseEffect(f, nil)` panics in dev mode |
| `tela.UseMount(f)`, `tela.UseEffectDo(f, deps...)`, `tela.UseUpdateEffect(f, deps...)` | Mount/unmount; an effect without cleanup; skip the first build |
| `tela.UseLayoutEffect(f, deps...)` | After layout, before paint: measure, scroll into view (the frame is painted scrolled) |
| `tela.UseMemo(compute, deps...)`, `tela.UseOnce(init)` | Cached value; computed once |
| `tela.UseCallback(fn)` | A stable comparable `tela.Callback[F]`; call `cb.Fn()`. Keeps props comparable |
| `r := tela.UseRef(init)` | `r.Current` persists, no rebuild |
| `el := tela.UseElementRef()` + `Ref(el)` | `el.Focus()`, `Blur`, `Click`, `Bounds()`, `ScrollTo/ScrollBy`, `ScrollIntoView()`, `ScrollToIndex(i, tela.AlignEnd)`, `Value()`, `Select()` |
| `tela.UseID()` | A stable unique id (label `For` + input `ID`) |
| `ctx := tela.CreateContext(def)` (package level), `ctx.Provider(v, children...)`, `tela.UseContext(ctx)` | Context; only readers rebuild |
| `v := tela.UseValue(init)` | Observable value: `v.Get()` in build rebuilds; read in a `...Fn` style prop (`tela.WidthFn`, `HeightFn`, `TranslateFn`, `OpacityFn`, `BgFn`, `TextColorFn`) or `TextFn` it only relayouts/repaints. `v.Set` from any goroutine |
| `tela.UseInterval(d, f)`, `tela.UseTimeout(d, f, deps...)` | On the frame clock, no goroutine. `d <= 0` pauses/cancels; a new `d` or deps restarts the timeout |
| `tela.UseGo(func(ctx context.Context), deps...)` | Background goroutine, cancelled when deps change or on unmount; update the UI through setters |
| `tela.UseSpring(target, opts...)`, `tela.UseTween(target, opts...)` | A `*tela.Value[T]` that animates toward `target` (float32, Color, Point, Size, Rect); feed it to a `...Fn` prop |
| `tela.UsePresence()`, `tela.UsePresenceTween()` | A component's own exit animation inside `h.Presence` |
| `tela.UseColorScheme()`, `tela.UseTheme()`, `tela.UseDirection()`, `tela.UseReducedMotion()` | Environment; `tela.SetColorScheme(tela.Dark)` switches the app |
| `kit.UseToast()`, `kit.UseStyle()` | Toast handle (under a `kit.Toaster`); the active kit recipe |

A custom hook is a function named `UseXxx`/`useXxx` that calls hooks. `tela.Post(f)` runs `f` on the UI thread from any goroutine.

```go
type action struct {
	kind string
	text string
}

func reduce(items []string, a action) []string {
	switch a.kind {
	case "add":
		return append(append([]string(nil), items...), a.text)
	case "clear":
		return nil
	}
	return items
}

var Mode = tela.CreateContext("light")

func DarkNotes() tela.Node { return Mode.Provider("dark", Notes()) }

func Notes() tela.Node { return tela.C(notes) }

func notes() tela.Node {
	items, dispatch := tela.UseReducer(reduce, []string{"Buy milk"})
	draft, setDraft := tela.UseState("")
	last := tela.UseElementRef()
	tela.UseLayoutEffect(func() func() {
		last.ScrollIntoView() // the frame that shows a new note shows it in view
		return nil
	}, len(items))
	mode := tela.UseContext(Mode)
	return Div(Class("flex h-80 flex-col gap-3 p-4"),
		P(Class("text-xs text-muted-foreground"), Textf("Mode: %s", mode)),
		Div(Class("flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-1 overflow-y-auto"),
			MapIndex(items, func(i int, s string) tela.Node {
				return P(Key(i), If(i == len(items)-1, Ref(last)), Class("text-sm"), Text(s))
			})),
		kit.Input{Placeholder: "New note", AriaLabel: "New note", Value: &draft, OnValueChange: setDraft.Set},
		kit.Button{Disabled: draft == "", Children: Text("Add"), OnClick: func() {
			dispatch.Dispatch(action{kind: "add", text: draft})
			setDraft.Set("")
		}})
}
```

Smooth values without rebuilds:

```go
func Drawer(open bool) tela.Node {
	target := float32(-320)
	if open {
		target = 0
	}
	x := tela.UseSpring(target) // starts at the target, then springs to new targets
	return Div(Class("fixed inset-y-0 left-0 w-80 border-r border-border bg-background p-6 shadow-xl"),
		Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (float32, float32) { return x.Get(), 0 })), // repaints only
		Text("Menu"))
}

func Download() tela.Node {
	progress := tela.UseValue(float32(0))
	tela.UseGo(func(ctx context.Context) {
		for i := 1; i <= 10 && ctx.Err() == nil; i++ {
			time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
			progress.Set(float32(i) / 10)
		}
	}, tela.Once)
	return Div(Class("h-2 w-64 overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-muted"),
		Div(Class("h-full bg-primary"), Style(tela.WidthFn(func() float32 { return 256 * progress.Get() }))))
}
```

## 5. Styling

Classes are Tailwind CSS v4's, verbatim, parsed into typed styles. If you would write it in React + Tailwind v4, write the same here. Order: element defaults, then classes in order (a later class wins over an earlier one that sets the same property; `Class` may repeat and takes several strings), then `Style(...)` props. No cascade, no selectors, no stylesheet. Everything is `border-box`. `Div` is `display: block`, like HTML.

**Supported:** spacing (`p-4`, `px-6`, `m-auto`, `gap-3`, `space-y-4`), sizing (`w-64`, `w-full`, `max-w-3xl`, `min-h-screen`, `size-8`, `h-[72px]`, `aspect-video`), flex (`flex`, `flex-col`, `items-center`, `justify-between`, `flex-1`, `shrink-0`, `grow`, `basis-1/3`, `flex-wrap`, `order-*`), grid (`grid grid-cols-3`, `grid-cols-[200px_1fr]`, `col-span-2`, `auto-rows-*`, `place-items-center`), positioning (`relative`, `absolute`, `fixed`, `sticky top-0`, `inset-0`, `z-10`), overflow and scrolling (`overflow-y-auto`, `overscroll-contain`, `scroll-smooth`), colors with opacity (`bg-white/15`, `text-zinc-500`, `bg-[#1e1e2e]`), borders (`border`, `border-b`, `border-border`, `rounded-xl`, `rounded-t-lg`), `ring-*`, `ring-offset-*`, `outline-*`, shadows (`shadow-sm`...`shadow-2xl`, `shadow-xs`, `inset-shadow-*`), gradients (`bg-linear-to-br from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500`, `bg-radial`, `bg-conic`), typography (`text-sm`, `font-semibold`, `tracking-tight`, `leading-6`, `truncate`, `line-clamp-2`, `text-balance`, `tabular-nums`, `uppercase`, `font-mono`, `font-['Family']`, `whitespace-pre`, `whitespace-nowrap`, `break-words`), effects (`opacity-50`, `blur-sm`, `backdrop-blur`, `drop-shadow-*`, `mix-blend-*`, masks), transforms (`translate-x-2`, `scale-95`, `rotate-45`, `origin-*`; 2D only), transitions (`transition`, `transition-colors`, `duration-200`, `ease-out`, `delay-*`), `animate-spin`/`pulse`/`ping`/`bounce` (also `animate-[bounce_1s_150ms_infinite]`), `cursor-pointer`, `pointer-events-none`, `select-none`, `sr-only`, `field-sizing-content`, background images (`bg-[url(img/hero.jpg)] bg-cover`, files registered with `tela.Assets(fsys)`), `[clip-path:circle(50%)]`, arbitrary values (`w-[calc(50%-8px)]`, `top-[3px]`, `grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fill,minmax(200px,1fr))]`). Units: `px`, `rem`, `em`, `%`, `vw`, `vh`, `fr`, `ch`. `calc()` only as `min()`, `max()`, `clamp()` and `a ± b`.

**Variants** (stack them: `dark:md:hover:bg-zinc-800`):
- State: `hover:` `active:` `focus:` `focus-visible:` `focus-within:` `disabled:` `enabled:` `checked:`, text fields `placeholder:` `invalid:` `read-only:` `placeholder-shown:` `selection:`.
- ARIA: `aria-checked:` `aria-selected:` `aria-expanded:` `aria-pressed:` `aria-invalid:` `aria-disabled:` `aria-busy:` `aria-hidden:` `aria-required:` `aria-readonly:` (they match the element's own `h.Aria...(true)` prop), `aria-[current=page]:` (also `step`, `location`, `date`, `time`, `true`; there is no bare `aria-current:`), `aria-[sort=ascending]:`/`descending`.
- Structure: `first:` `last:` `only:` `odd:` `even:`; `group` + `group-hover:`/`group-focus-within:`/`group-aria-*:` on descendants; `peer` + `peer-checked:`/`peer-invalid:`... on following siblings (no named groups).
- Environment: `dark:`, `sm:` `md:` `lg:` `xl:` `2xl:` (window at least 640/768/1024/1280/1536 px), `max-md:` ..., `min-[600px]:`, `max-[40rem]:`, `motion-reduce:`, `motion-safe:`, `rtl:`/`ltr:`, `starting:` (entrance: the style a newly shown element transitions from, CSS `@starting-style`).

```go
func NavLink(label string, current bool, onClick func()) tela.Node {
	page := ""
	if current {
		page = "page"
	}
	return Button(AriaCurrent(page), OnClick(onClick),
		Class("group flex h-9 w-full items-center gap-3 rounded-md px-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground transition-colors",
			"hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground",
			"aria-[current=page]:bg-accent aria-[current=page]:font-medium aria-[current=page]:text-foreground"),
		Icon(lucide.Bell, Class("size-4 group-hover:text-foreground")), Text(label))
}

func Toast(message string) tela.Node {
	// Fades and slides in when it appears; under Presence, Exit classes run when it is removed.
	return Div(Class("rounded-lg border border-border bg-popover px-4 py-3 text-sm shadow-lg transition duration-300",
		"starting:translate-y-2 starting:opacity-0"), Exit("translate-y-2 opacity-0"), Role("status"), Text(message))
}

func Responsive() tela.Node {
	return Div(Class("grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 p-4 md:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-3"),
		Div(Class("h-24 rounded-xl bg-linear-to-br from-sky-400 to-indigo-600 shadow-lg dark:from-sky-600 dark:to-indigo-900")),
		Div(Class("h-24 rounded-xl bg-white/60 ring-1 ring-black/5 backdrop-blur dark:bg-white/5 dark:ring-white/10")))
}
```

**Theme tokens** (shadcn/ui names) work in every color utility (`bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `fill-`, `stroke-`, `shadow-`...), with opacity (`bg-primary/90`, `ring-ring/50`) and variants, and follow the color scheme by themselves: no `dark:` pairs needed. Tokens: `background`, `foreground`, `card`, `card-foreground`, `popover`, `popover-foreground`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `secondary`, `secondary-foreground`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `accent`, `accent-foreground`, `destructive`, `border`, `input`, `ring`, `chart-1`..`chart-5`. Give the window `RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground"`. Palette colors (`bg-zinc-900`) do not follow the scheme: pair them with `dark:`.

`kit.Theme()` is shadcn's neutral theme with its 10 px radius (`rounded-lg` = 10 px, `rounded-md` 8, `rounded-xl` 14); `tela.DefaultTheme()` has the same colors with Tailwind's radius scale. Change colors, add your own tokens, alias class combinations:

```go
var brandTheme = func() tela.Theme {
	t := kit.Theme()
	t.Colors["primary"] = tela.SchemeColor{Light: tela.Hex("#4f46e5"), Dark: tela.Hex("#818cf8")}
	t.Colors["primary-foreground"] = tela.SchemeColor{Light: tela.Hex("#ffffff"), Dark: tela.Hex("#1e1b4b")}
	t.Colors["brand"] = tela.SchemeColor{Light: tela.Hex("#7c3aed"), Dark: tela.Hex("#a78bfa")} // bg-brand, text-brand...
	t.FontSans = "Geist"                                                                         // a system font; Inter is the fallback
	return t
}()

var BrandApp = tela.App{
	Title: "Notes", Theme: &brandTheme, RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground",
	ClassAliases: map[string]string{
		"text-muted": "text-sm text-muted-foreground",
		"eyebrow":    "text-xs font-semibold tracking-wide text-brand uppercase",
	},
	Root: P(Class("eyebrow"), Text("Notes")),
}
```

Colors in Go: `tela.Hex("#4f46e5")`, `tela.RGB`, `tela.RGBA(r, g, b, a)`, `tela.OKLCH(l, c, h)`, `tela.UseTheme().Color("primary")`. `h.Scheme(tela.Dark)` gives a subtree its own scheme (a dark sidebar in a light app). `tela.SetColorScheme(tela.Dark)` switches the app's scheme at run time, and `tela.SetTheme(t)` its theme: an accent picker copies `kit.Theme()`, sets `t.Colors["primary"]` (and `ring`) and calls `tela.SetTheme(t)`, so every `bg-primary` follows.

**Fonts:** `font-sans` (Inter, the default), `font-mono` (JetBrains Mono, embedded), `font-serif`, or a named family `font-['Fira_Code',monospace]` (`_` for spaces). Named families come from the system when the app runs; `tela snapshot`, `tela mcp` and tests use only the embedded fonts, so there they fall back to Inter or JetBrains Mono. A theme's `FontSans`/`FontMono` rename the defaults.

**Icons:** `Icon(lucide.Settings, Class("size-4"))`. An icon is 1em square (follows `text-*` size) unless sized, colored by the text color (`text-muted-foreground`), `stroke-[1.5]` thins it; decorative unless it has an `AriaLabel`. Lucide names are the file names in CamelCase (`arrow-up-right` is `lucide.ArrowUpRight`). Your own SVGs: `tela.Icon{SVG: "<svg ...>"}`, `tela.MustSVG(data)`, or `tela icons gen -pkg icons -o ./icons ./svg` for a whole directory.

**Not implemented** (you get a dev error that says what to use): floats and `clear` (use flex/grid); margin collapsing (use `gap`/`space-y-*`); `display: table` and `border-collapse` (use `kit.Table` or grid); `divide-*` (borders on the children, `border-t first:border-t-0`); `space-*-reverse`; `columns-*`; pseudo-elements `before:` `after:` `marker:` `file:` (use nodes); `data-*:`, `has-*:`, `not-*:`, `nth-*:`, `*:`, `[&...]:`, `@container`/`@md:`, `print:`, `supports-*:`; `var()`/CSS variables (use tokens); arbitrary properties other than `[clip-path:...]`; 3D transforms; `scroll-snap`, `scroll-m-*`; `text-indent`; `hyphens`; `accent-*`; `resize`; `bg-fixed`; `vertical-align` on spans; custom `@keyframes` (use the `animate-*` classes, springs or `tela.Animate`); `content-box`.

## 6. kit: components in shadcn/ui's look

`kit` has 36 components with shadcn/ui's ("new-york-v4") look, built on the `aria` behavior hooks: keyboard, focus and roles are done. Use them for every control; build layout and decoration with `h` elements and classes around them.

**Rules that hold for every component:**
- Each is a struct; its fields are its props. `Class` adds classes to the root after the component's own (last wins: `Class: "w-full"` overrides); parts have `...Class` fields (`HeaderClass`, `ContentClass`, `ItemClass`...). `Props` takes one more `h` prop for the root (`Props: TestID("save")`; several: `tela.MergeProps(TestID("x"), AutoComplete("email"))`).
- Content is `Children tela.Component`; multi-part components have slots (`kit.Card{Title, Description, Action, Children, Footer}`). Text-only slots for assistive technologies are strings (`kit.Field{Label, Description, Error}`).
- A kit component is a `tela.Component`, not a `tela.Node`: return it from a function as `Fragment(kit.Button{...})`.
- Values: controlled `Value *T` + `OnValueChange func(T)` (`Checked *bool` + `OnCheckedChange`, `Open *bool` + `OnOpenChange`, `Pressed`), or uncontrolled `DefaultValue`/`DefaultChecked`/`DefaultOpen`. Choices among keys are generic: `kit.Select[string]`, `Value *K`, `DefaultValue *K` (write `new("pro")`: `new` takes a value since Go 1.26).
- `Variant`: `kit.Default` (zero), `kit.Secondary`, `kit.Outline`, `kit.Ghost`, `kit.Destructive`, `kit.Link` (and `kit.TabsLine` for Tabs). `Size`: empty is the default size, then `kit.Xs`, `kit.Sm`, `kit.Lg`, and for icon-only buttons `kit.Icon`, `kit.IconXs`, `kit.IconSm`, `kit.IconLg`. `Orientation`: `kit.Horizontal`, `kit.Vertical`. An undefined variant or size panics in dev mode with the valid ones.
- Overlays (`Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, `Popover`, `Tooltip`, menus, pickers) take a `Trigger`: a `kit.Button{...}`, or any element through `kit.TriggerFunc(func(p tela.Prop) tela.Node { return Button(p, ...) })`. Put `Disabled` on the overlay, not on its trigger. A trigger takes one overlay.
- Icons are `tela.Icon` fields (`Button.Icon`, `IconEnd`), defaulting to Lucide's where shadcn draws one.
- Customize: theme tokens first; then recipes: `s := kit.DefaultStyle()`, edit class strings (`s.Card.Root += " shadow-lg"`, `s.Button.Variants["glass"] = "bg-white/10 text-white hover:bg-white/20"`), apply with `kit.StyleProvider{Style: &s, Children: ...}`; then per instance `Class`.

**Catalog** (key fields; nearly every component also has `Class` and `Props`):

- `kit.Button{Variant, Size, Icon, IconEnd, Type, Disabled, OnClick, AriaLabel, Children}`: `Type: "submit"` in a `Form`; icon-only buttons need `Size: kit.Icon` and `AriaLabel`.
- `kit.Badge{Variant, Icon, Children}`: a small label.
- `kit.Card{Title, Description, Action, Children, Footer, TitleLevel, HeaderClass, ContentClass, FooterClass}`: the surface; `TitleLevel: 2` makes the title an `h2`; `Action` sits at the header's end.
- `kit.Avatar{Src, Alt, Fallback, Size, FallbackClass}`: `Src: SrcPath("img/ada.png")`; `Fallback` initials.
- `kit.Separator{Orientation, Semantic}`: a 1 px line (`Semantic` puts it in the accessibility tree).
- `kit.Skeleton{Class}`: a pulsing placeholder (`Class: "h-4 w-40 rounded-md"`).
- `kit.Label{For, Disabled, Children}`: a styled label for a control with an `ID`.
- `kit.Input{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Type, Placeholder, Name, ID, AriaLabel, Disabled, ReadOnly, Invalid, AutoFocus, MaxLength}`.
- `kit.Textarea{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Placeholder, Rows, MaxLength, AriaLabel, Invalid}`.
- `kit.Field{Label, Description, Error, Invalid, Orientation, ControlAfter, Children, LabelClass, ContentClass}`: label, control, help and error wired together (`Error` marks the control invalid). One kit control per field. Its spacing, to match it in rows you build by hand: `gap-3` between label, control and description; in a horizontal field the label and description are a column with `gap-1.5`; the description is `text-sm text-muted-foreground`.
- `kit.FieldSet{Legend, LegendVariant, Description, Children, LegendClass, ContentClass}`: a named group; names a `RadioGroup`/`ToggleGroup` inside. `LegendVariant: kit.LegendVariantLabel` is label-sized, the default `kit.LegendVariantLegend` a title.
- `kit.Checkbox{Checked, DefaultChecked, OnCheckedChange, Disabled, Required, Invalid, ID, AriaLabel}`.
- `kit.Switch{Checked, DefaultChecked, OnCheckedChange, Size, Disabled, ID, AriaLabel, ThumbClass}`.
- `kit.RadioGroup[K]{Items, Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Orientation, Disabled, AriaLabel, Render, OptionClass}`: options are `kit.RadioItem[K]{Value, Label, Description, Disabled}`; `Render func(kit.RadioItem[K], kit.RadioState) tela.Node` draws an option yourself (cards).
- `kit.RadioState{Checked, Disabled, Invalid, ID, Props, Indicator}`: what `Render` gets: put `Props` on the one element that is the radio; `Indicator` is the default circle.
- `kit.Toggle{Pressed, DefaultPressed, OnPressedChange, Variant, Size, Icon, AriaLabel, Children}`: a button that stays pressed.
- `kit.ToggleGroup[K]{Items, Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Multiple, Selected, OnSelectionChange, DisallowEmptySelection, Variant, Size, Spacing, AriaLabel, ItemClass}`: segmented control; items `kit.ToggleGroupItem[K]{Value, Label, Icon, AriaLabel, Disabled}`.
- `kit.Slider{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Values, OnValuesChange, Min, Max, Step, Orientation, Disabled, AriaLabel, FormatValue}`: `Value *float64`; `DefaultValue: new(50.0)`; `FormatValue func(float64) string` is the value as read aloud (aria-valuetext), not drawn: show the value yourself (`Textf("%g px", v)`).
- `kit.Progress{Value, Max, Indeterminate, AriaLabel}`: `Value` is a plain number (0 to `Max`, 100 by default).
- `kit.Select[K]{Items, Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Placeholder, Size, Disabled, Invalid, AriaLabel, ID}`: items `kit.SelectItem[K]{Value, Label, Icon, Disabled, Group}`; its trigger is a `button` named "chosen label + field label".
- `kit.Tabs[K]{Tabs, Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Orientation, Variant, AriaLabel, ListClass, TriggerClass, ContentClass}`: `kit.Tab[K]{Value, Label, Icon, Disabled, Content}`; only the selected panel is built.
- `kit.Table[T]{Rows, RowKey, Columns, Sort, DefaultSort, OnSortChange, Selected, RowProps, Caption, AriaLabel, Empty}`: columns `kit.Column[T]{Header, Cell, Sort, Width, Align, Sticky, Footer}`; `Width string` is the column's grid track (`"200px"`, `"1fr"`, `"auto"`, `"minmax(120px, 1fr)"`); `Align: kit.AlignRight`; a `Sort` func makes a header sortable.
- `kit.Dialog{Trigger, Title, Description, Children, Footer, Open, DefaultOpen, OnOpenChange, HideClose, AriaLabel}`: modal; Escape and the scrim close it.
- `kit.AlertDialog{Trigger, Title, Description, Cancel, Action, Destructive, OnAction, OnCancel, Open, OnOpenChange, Disabled}`: a confirmation; `Cancel`/`Action` are labels (default "Cancel"/"Continue").
- `kit.Popover{Trigger, Children, Placement, Align, Offset, Modal, AriaLabel, Open, OnOpenChange}`: non-modal panel; `Placement: "top"`, `Align: "start"`.
- `kit.TitleBar{Variant, Title, Leading, Children, Trailing, ControlsSide, HideMinimize, HideMaximize, State, TitleClass}`: the title bar of a `Frameless` window (or one with `tela.UseWindow().State().ClientSideDecorations`): a drag area (`h.WindowDrag`) with a title, slots and the window controls at the platform's side; buttons and fields in the slots stay clickable. Looks `kit.Windows`, `kit.GNOME`, `kit.MacOS` (default by OS); it dims when the window is unfocused and drops its outline when maximized. Put it at the top of a flex column.
- `kit.WindowControls{Variant, HideMinimize, HideMaximize, State, MinimizeLabel, MaximizeLabel, RestoreLabel, CloseLabel}`: minimize, maximize/restore and close as real buttons (named "Minimize", "Maximize"/"Restore", "Close") that act on click; `TitleBar` draws them, so use this alone only to place them yourself.
- `kit.Tooltip{Trigger, Content, Placement, Delay, Disabled}`: on hover or keyboard focus; describes its trigger.
- `kit.DropdownMenu[K]{Trigger, Items, OnSelect, Placement, Align, AriaLabel, Open, OnOpenChange}`: items `kit.MenuItem[K]{Kind, Key, Label, Icon, Shortcut, Variant, Disabled, OnSelect, Checked, DefaultChecked, OnCheckedChange, Items}`; `Kind`: `kit.MenuPlain` (zero), `kit.MenuCheckbox`, `kit.MenuRadioGroup`, `kit.MenuLabel`, `kit.MenuSeparator`, `kit.MenuGroup`. No submenus.
- `kit.ContextMenu[K]{Children, Items, OnSelect, AriaLabel, Disabled}`: right click (or long press) on `Children`.
- `kit.Menubar[K]{Menus, OnSelect, AriaLabel}`: menus `kit.MenubarMenu[K]{Key, Label, Items, Disabled}`.
- `kit.Toaster{Children, Position, Duration, VisibleToasts, CloseButton}`: put once around the app; any component below calls `toast := kit.UseToast()` then `toast.Success(title, opts...)`, `Error`, `Info`, `Warning`, `Loading`, `Show`, `Dismiss(id)`; options `kit.ToastDescription(text)`, `kit.ToastAction(label, fn)`, `kit.ToastDuration(d)`, `kit.ToastReplace(id)`. Safe from any goroutine.
- `kit.Calendar{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Min, Max, IsDateUnavailable, VisibleMonths}`: one `aria.Date` (comparable day, zero = none; `aria.Today()`).
- `kit.RangeCalendar{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, VisibleMonths}`: an `aria.DateRange`.
- `kit.DatePicker{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Placeholder, Min, Max}`: an outline button that opens a calendar.
- `kit.DateRangePicker{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Placeholder}`: the same for a range.
- `kit.ColorPicker{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, OnValueCommit, Alpha, Swatches}`: a `tela.Color` (`DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))`).
- `kit.ColorInput{Value, DefaultValue, OnValueChange, Swatches}`: the picker behind a button.
- `kit.StyleProvider{Style, Children}`: applies an edited `kit.DefaultStyle()` to a subtree.

**Patterns.** A form card with fields, errors and a submit:

```go
func Profile() tela.Node { return tela.C(profile) }

func profile() tela.Node {
	name, setName := tela.UseState("Ada Lovelace")
	email, setEmail := tela.UseState("ada@example")
	bio, setBio := tela.UseState("")
	emailError := ""
	if !strings.Contains(email, ".") {
		emailError = "Enter a valid e-mail address."
	}
	return Fragment(kit.Card{
		Class: "w-full max-w-md", TitleLevel: 2,
		Title:       Text("Profile"),
		Description: Text("This is how others see you."),
		Action:      kit.Badge{Variant: kit.Secondary, Children: Text("Public")},
		Children: Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-5"),
			kit.Field{Label: "Name", Children: kit.Input{Value: &name, OnValueChange: setName.Set}},
			kit.Field{Label: "E-mail", Description: "We never share it.", Error: emailError,
				Children: kit.Input{Type: "email", Value: &email, OnValueChange: setEmail.Set}},
			kit.Field{Label: "Bio", Children: kit.Textarea{Rows: 3, Placeholder: "A few words", Value: &bio, OnValueChange: setBio.Set}}),
		FooterClass: "justify-end gap-2",
		Footer: Fragment(
			kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: Text("Cancel")},
			kit.Button{Disabled: emailError != "", Children: Text("Save")}),
	})
}
```

Switch rows, a radio group named by a legend, radio cards, a select, a segmented control:

```go
func Preferences() tela.Node { return tela.C(preferences) }

func preferences() tela.Node {
	digest, setDigest := tela.UseState(true)
	plan, setPlan := tela.UseState("pro")
	size, setSize := tela.UseState("md")
	view, setView := tela.UseState("list")
	plans := []kit.RadioItem[string]{
		{Value: "free", Label: "Free", Description: "Up to 3 projects."},
		{Value: "pro", Label: "Pro", Description: "Unlimited projects."},
	}
	return Div(Class("flex max-w-lg flex-col gap-6"),
		// A switch row: text first, the switch at the end.
		kit.Field{Orientation: kit.Horizontal, ControlAfter: true, Class: "items-center gap-6",
			Label: "Weekly digest", Description: "A summary every Monday.",
			Children: kit.Switch{Checked: &digest, OnCheckedChange: setDigest.Set}},
		// The legend names the group: no AriaLabel needed.
		kit.FieldSet{Legend: "Plan", LegendVariant: kit.LegendVariantLabel,
			Children: kit.RadioGroup[string]{Items: plans, Value: &plan, OnValueChange: setPlan.Set}},
		kit.Field{Label: "Text size", Children: kit.Select[string]{Class: "w-40", Value: &size, OnValueChange: setSize.Set,
			Items: []kit.SelectItem[string]{{Value: "sm", Label: "Small"}, {Value: "md", Label: "Medium"}, {Value: "lg", Label: "Large"}}}},
		kit.FieldSet{Legend: "View", LegendVariant: kit.LegendVariantLabel,
			Children: kit.ToggleGroup[string]{Variant: kit.Outline, DisallowEmptySelection: true, Value: &view, OnValueChange: setView.Set,
				Items: []kit.ToggleGroupItem[string]{{Value: "list", Label: "List"}, {Value: "grid", Label: "Grid"}}}},
		// Radio cards: Render draws each option; st.Props makes the button the radio.
		kit.RadioGroup[string]{AriaLabel: "Plan cards", Items: plans, Value: &plan, OnValueChange: setPlan.Set, Class: "grid-cols-2",
			Render: func(o kit.RadioItem[string], st kit.RadioState) tela.Node {
				return Button(Key(o.Value), st.Props,
					Class("flex flex-col items-start gap-1 rounded-lg border border-border p-4 text-left transition-colors hover:bg-accent",
						"aria-checked:border-primary aria-checked:ring-1 aria-checked:ring-primary"),
					Div(Class("flex items-center gap-2 text-sm font-medium"), st.Indicator, Text(o.Label)),
					P(Class("text-sm text-muted-foreground"), Text(o.Description)))
			}},
	)
}
```

Tabs, buttons, an alert dialog, a toast, a tooltip, a dropdown menu, an avatar:

```go
func Account() tela.Component { return kit.Toaster{Children: tela.C(account)} }

func account() tela.Node {
	toast := kit.UseToast()
	menu := []kit.MenuItem[string]{
		{Kind: kit.MenuLabel, Label: "My account"},
		{Key: "edit", Label: "Edit", Icon: lucide.Pencil, Shortcut: "Ctrl+E"},
		{Kind: kit.MenuSeparator},
		{Key: "logout", Label: "Log out", Icon: lucide.LogOut, Variant: kit.Destructive},
	}
	return Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-6 p-8"),
		Div(Class("flex items-center gap-3"),
			kit.Avatar{Fallback: "AL", Size: kit.Lg},
			Div(Class("flex flex-1 flex-col"), Span(Class("font-medium"), Text("Ada Lovelace")),
				Span(Class("text-sm text-muted-foreground"), Text("ada@example.com"))),
			kit.Tooltip{Content: Text("Invite a teammate"),
				Trigger: kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Size: kit.Icon, Icon: lucide.Plus, AriaLabel: "Invite"}},
			kit.DropdownMenu[string]{Align: "end", Items: menu, OnSelect: func(k string) { toast.Info("Chose " + k) },
				Trigger: kit.Button{Variant: kit.Ghost, Size: kit.Icon, Icon: lucide.Ellipsis, AriaLabel: "More"}}),
		kit.Separator{},
		kit.Tabs[string]{DefaultValue: new("general"), Tabs: []kit.Tab[string]{
			{Value: "general", Label: "General", Content: Div(Class("flex gap-2 pt-2"),
				kit.Button{Icon: lucide.Check, Children: Text("Save"),
					OnClick: func() { toast.Success("Saved", kit.ToastDescription("Your changes are live.")) }},
				kit.Button{Variant: kit.Secondary, Children: Text("Preview")},
				kit.Button{Variant: kit.Link, Children: Text("Learn more")})},
			{Value: "danger", Label: "Danger zone", Content: Div(Class("pt-2"),
				kit.AlertDialog{
					Trigger:     kit.Button{Variant: kit.Destructive, Icon: lucide.Trash2, Children: Text("Delete account")},
					Title:       Text("Delete your account?"),
					Description: Text("This cannot be undone."),
					Action:      Text("Delete"), Destructive: true,
					OnAction: func() { toast.Error("Account deleted") },
				})},
		}})
}
```

A table and a dialog with a form:

```go
type Invoice struct {
	ID, Status string
	Amount     float64
}

func Invoices(rows []Invoice) tela.Node {
	return Fragment(kit.Table[Invoice]{
		Rows: rows, RowKey: func(i Invoice) any { return i.ID }, Caption: "Recent invoices",
		Columns: []kit.Column[Invoice]{
			{Header: "Invoice", Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return Span(Class("font-medium"), Text(i.ID)) },
				Sort: func(a, b Invoice) int { return strings.Compare(a.ID, b.ID) }},
			{Header: "Status", Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return Fragment(kit.Badge{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: Text(i.Status)}) }},
			{Header: "Amount", Align: kit.AlignRight, Cell: func(i Invoice) tela.Node { return Textf("$%.2f", i.Amount) },
				Sort: func(a, b Invoice) int { return cmp.Compare(a.Amount, b.Amount) }},
		},
	})
}

func Rename() tela.Node { return tela.C(rename) }

func rename() tela.Node {
	open, setOpen := tela.UseState(false)
	name, setName := tela.UseState("Roadmap")
	return Fragment(kit.Dialog{
		Open: &open, OnOpenChange: setOpen.Set,
		Trigger:     kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Icon: lucide.Pencil, Children: Text("Rename")},
		Title:       Text("Rename project"),
		Description: Text("Pick a short, memorable name."),
		Children:    kit.Field{Label: "Name", Children: kit.Input{Value: &name, OnValueChange: setName.Set, AutoFocus: true}},
		Footer:      kit.Button{Disabled: name == "", OnClick: func() { setOpen.Set(false) }, Children: Text("Save")},
	})
}
```

An alert (there is no `kit.Alert`): a `Div` with `Role("alert")`:

```go
func ErrorAlert(title, detail string) tela.Node {
	return Div(Role("alert"),
		Class("flex flex-col gap-0.5 rounded-lg border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/5 px-4 py-3 text-sm text-destructive"),
		Div(Class("font-medium"), Text(title)),
		Div(Class("text-destructive/80"), Text(detail)))
}
```

## 7. A complete settings screen

This is `examples/llms/settings/main.go` (its tests and goldens are next to it): an app shell with a sidebar whose current item has `AriaCurrent("page")`, a header with Save, a card of switch rows, a card with a `FieldSet` of radio cards and a horizontal `Field` with a `Select`; Save applies the theme with `tela.SetColorScheme` and shows a toast. It uses tokens only, so dark mode needs no `dark:` class. Copy its structure: `max-w-3xl` centered content, `gap-6` between cards, `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight` title with a `text-sm text-muted-foreground` subtitle, rows separated by `border-t first:border-t-0`.

```go
// Command settings is the worked example of docs/llms.txt, which shows this
// file verbatim: an app shell with a sidebar and a settings page on kit.
package main

import (
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/kit"

	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/icons/lucide"
)

// Prefs is the whole form: comparable, so prefs != saved means "unsaved".
type Prefs struct {
	Email, Push, Digest bool
	Theme, Language     string
}

var defaults = Prefs{Email: true, Push: true, Theme: "system", Language: "en"}

type navItem struct {
	Label string
	Icon  tela.Icon
}

var nav = []navItem{
	{"Dashboard", lucide.LayoutDashboard}, {"Projects", lucide.FolderKanban},
	{"Team", lucide.Users}, {"Settings", lucide.Settings},
}

var themes = []kit.RadioItem[string]{
	{Value: "light", Label: "Light"}, {Value: "dark", Label: "Dark"}, {Value: "system", Label: "System"},
}

var themeIcons = map[string]tela.Icon{"light": lucide.Sun, "dark": lucide.Moon, "system": lucide.Monitor}

var schemes = map[string]tela.ColorScheme{"light": tela.Light, "dark": tela.Dark, "system": tela.System}

var languages = []kit.SelectItem[string]{
	{Value: "en", Label: "English"}, {Value: "es", Label: "Español"},
	{Value: "fr", Label: "Français"}, {Value: "de", Label: "Deutsch"},
}

// Settings is the screen; tela.C gives settings its own hook state.
func Settings() tela.Node { return tela.C(settings) }

func settings() tela.Node {
	page, setPage := tela.UseState("Settings")
	prefs, setPrefs := tela.UseState(defaults)
	saved, setSaved := tela.UseState(defaults)
	toast := kit.UseToast()

	edit := func(f func(p *Prefs)) { setPrefs.Update(func(p Prefs) Prefs { f(&p); return p }) }
	save := func() {
		setSaved.Set(prefs)
		tela.SetColorScheme(schemes[prefs.Theme])
		toast.Success("Settings saved", kit.ToastDescription("Your preferences were updated."))
	}
	row := func(label, hint string, on bool, set func(p *Prefs, on bool)) tela.Node {
		return Fragment(kit.Field{
			Orientation: kit.Horizontal, ControlAfter: true, Label: label, Description: hint,
			Class:    "items-center gap-6 border-t border-border py-4 first:border-t-0 first:pt-0 last:pb-0",
			Children: kit.Switch{Checked: &on, OnCheckedChange: func(v bool) { edit(func(p *Prefs) { set(p, v) }) }},
		})
	}

	sidebar := Div(Role("navigation"), AriaLabel("Main"),
		Class("flex w-60 shrink-0 flex-col gap-1 border-r border-border bg-muted/40 p-3"),
		Div(Class("flex items-center gap-2.5 px-2 pt-1 pb-5"),
			Div(Class("flex size-8 items-center justify-center rounded-lg bg-primary text-primary-foreground"),
				Icon(lucide.Layers, Class("size-4"))),
			Span(Class("font-semibold tracking-tight"), Text("Acme"))),
		Map(nav, func(n navItem) tela.Node {
			current := ""
			if n.Label == page {
				current = "page"
			}
			return Button(Key(n.Label), AriaCurrent(current), OnClick(func() { setPage.Set(n.Label) }),
				Class("flex h-9 items-center gap-3 rounded-md px-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground transition-colors",
					"hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground",
					"aria-[current=page]:bg-accent aria-[current=page]:font-medium aria-[current=page]:text-foreground"),
				Icon(n.Icon, Class("size-4")), Text(n.Label))
		}),
		Div(Class("mt-auto flex items-center gap-3 border-t border-border px-2 pt-4"),
			kit.Avatar{Fallback: "AL"},
			Div(Class("flex min-w-0 flex-col text-sm"),
				Span(Class("font-medium"), Text("Ada Lovelace")),
				Span(Class("truncate text-xs text-muted-foreground"), Text("ada@example.com")))),
	)

	content := Div(Class("mx-auto flex max-w-3xl flex-col gap-6 px-8 py-8"),
		Div(Class("flex items-end justify-between gap-4"),
			Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-1"),
				H1(Class("text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight"), Text("Settings")),
				P(Class("text-sm text-muted-foreground"), Text("Manage your notifications and how Acme looks."))),
			kit.Button{Icon: lucide.Check, Disabled: prefs == saved, OnClick: save, Children: Text("Save changes")}),
		kit.Card{TitleLevel: 2, Title: Text("Notifications"), Description: Text("Choose what we tell you about."),
			Children: Div(Class("flex flex-col"),
				row("Email notifications", "A summary of activity in your workspace.", prefs.Email, func(p *Prefs, v bool) { p.Email = v }),
				row("Push notifications", "Mentions and replies, on your devices.", prefs.Push, func(p *Prefs, v bool) { p.Push = v }),
				row("Weekly digest", "A Monday recap of what your team shipped.", prefs.Digest, func(p *Prefs, v bool) { p.Digest = v }))},
		kit.Card{TitleLevel: 2, Title: Text("Appearance"), Description: Text("Applied when you save."),
			ContentClass: "flex flex-col gap-6",
			Children: Fragment(
				kit.FieldSet{Legend: "Theme", LegendVariant: kit.LegendVariantLabel,
					Children: kit.RadioGroup[string]{Items: themes, Render: themeCard, Class: "grid-cols-3",
						Value: &prefs.Theme, OnValueChange: func(v string) { edit(func(p *Prefs) { p.Theme = v }) }}},
				kit.Field{Orientation: kit.Horizontal, ControlAfter: true, Class: "items-center gap-6",
					Label: "Language", Description: "Used for dates, numbers and messages.",
					Children: kit.Select[string]{Items: languages, Class: "w-44",
						Value: &prefs.Language, OnValueChange: func(v string) { edit(func(p *Prefs) { p.Language = v }) }}})},
	)

	return Div(Class("flex h-screen"), sidebar,
		Div(Class("min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto"),
			IfElse(page == "Settings", content, Div(Class("flex h-full items-center justify-center text-sm text-muted-foreground"),
				Textf("%s is empty in this example.", page)))))
}

// themeCard draws one theme option; st.Props makes the button the radio.
func themeCard(o kit.RadioItem[string], st kit.RadioState) tela.Node {
	return Button(Key(o.Value), st.Props,
		Class("flex items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-lg border border-border bg-card px-3 py-2.5 text-sm font-medium shadow-xs transition-colors",
			"hover:bg-accent focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring/50",
			"aria-checked:border-primary aria-checked:bg-accent aria-checked:ring-1 aria-checked:ring-primary"),
		Icon(themeIcons[o.Value], Class("size-4")), Text(o.Label))
}

var theme = kit.Theme()

// App is the window; tela snapshot, tela mcp and the tests mount it too.
var App = tela.App{
	Title: "Settings", Width: 1040, Height: 800,
	Theme: &theme, RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground",
	Root: kit.Toaster{Children: Settings()},
}

func main() { tela.Main(App) }
```

Its aria snapshot (`tela inspect`, or the `snapshot` tool, which adds refs):

```yaml
- navigation "Main":
  - text: Acme
  - button "Dashboard"
  - button "Projects"
  - button "Team"
  - button "Settings"
  - text: AL Ada Lovelace ada@example.com
- heading "Settings" [level=1]
- paragraph: Manage your notifications and how Acme looks.
- button "Save changes" [disabled]
- heading "Notifications" [level=2]
- text: Choose what we tell you about.
- group:
  - text: Email notifications
  - paragraph: A summary of activity in your workspace.
  - switch "Email notifications" [checked]
...
- group "Theme":
  - text: Theme
  - radiogroup "Theme":
    - radio "Light"
    - radio "Dark"
    - radio "System" [checked]
- group:
  - text: Language
  - paragraph: Used for dates, numbers and messages.
  - button "English Language": English
- region "Notifications"
```

(`aria-current` is not printed in snapshots, as in Playwright; `region "Notifications"` is the Toaster's.)

## 8. Windows and desktop services

A window is state, like a dialog: a `tela.Window{...}` in the tree opens a window while it is mounted and closes it when it unmounts. All windows share one component tree, so a child window sees the state and contexts of the component that declares it (its `Root` is built by that component). Each window has its own layout, focus, hover and overlays. OS services (file dialogs, message boxes, notifications, tray, app folders, settings) are in package `github.com/kuronosu/tela/desktop`.

- `tela.Window{Title, Width, Height, MinWidth..MaxHeight, FixedSize, Frameless, AlwaysOnTop, Modal, Hidden, Icon, RootClass, Placement, OnClose, Root}`. Keep "is it open" in `UseState` and render `If(open, tela.Window{...})`. `OnClose` runs when the user asks to close (close button, Alt+F4, `Close()`): set the state to false there. **A nil `OnClose` ignores the request**: the window cannot be closed (dev mode warns). `FixedSize`, `Frameless`, `Modal` and `Placement` are read when the window opens; `Hidden` keeps it open, with its state.
- `tela.App` has the same fields for the main window, plus `AppID` and `OnClose func(tela.WindowHandle)`: nil quits when the main window closes; `func(w tela.WindowHandle) { w.Hide() }` keeps the app running (with a `desktop.Tray` as the way back). `tela.Quit()` ends the app from any goroutine; `tela.OpenURL(url)` and `tela.OpenPath(path)` open the default application.
- `tela.UseWindow()` returns the `tela.WindowHandle` of the window the component renders in: `Minimize`, `Maximize`, `Unmaximize`, `ToggleMaximize`, `SetFullscreen(bool)`, `Hide`, `Show`, `Focus`, `Close`, `State()` (`Maximized`, `Fullscreen`, `Minimized`, `Focused`, `Hidden`, `ClientSideDecorations`; reading it rebuilds the component when it changes) and `Placement()`. Requests are safe from any goroutine; the OS may refuse one (a tiling window manager does not maximize). In `tela snapshot` there is no window and the handle does nothing.
- **Custom title bar:** `Frameless: true`, and `kit.TitleBar{Title: Text("Notes"), Leading, Children, Trailing}` at the top of a flex column: it is the drag area and draws minimize, maximize and close (`kit.WindowControls`) in the OS's look; buttons and fields in its slots stay clickable. Without `kit`, mark the bar `h.WindowDrag()`, a plain area inside it that must not drag `h.WindowNoDrag()`, and real buttons `h.WindowControl(tela.WindowMinimize|WindowMaximize|WindowClose)` (with an `AriaLabel`); the OS does the move, the double click and the window menu. A Wayland desktop without server-side decorations reports `State().ClientSideDecorations`: draw the bar then.

```go
package notes

import (
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/desktop"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/kit"
)

var theme = kit.Theme()

// App: PersistApp reopens the main window where the user left it.
var App = desktop.PersistApp(tela.App{
	AppID: "com.example.notes", Title: "Notes", Width: 900, Height: 640,
	Frameless: true, Theme: &theme, RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground",
	Root: Notes{},
})

type Notes struct{}

func (Notes) Build() tela.Node {
	prefs, setPrefs := tela.UseState(false)
	return Div(Class("flex h-screen flex-col"),
		kit.TitleBar{Title: Text("Notes")},
		Div(Class("min-h-0 grow p-4"),
			kit.Button{Variant: kit.Outline, Children: Text("Preferences"),
				OnClick: func() { setPrefs.Set(true) }},
			If(prefs, tela.Window{
				Title: "Preferences", Width: 420, Height: 240, Modal: true,
				OnClose: func() { setPrefs.Set(false) },
				Root:    Preferences{},
			}),
		))
}

// Preferences is the content of the second window.
type Preferences struct{}

func (Preferences) Build() tela.Node {
	win := tela.UseWindow()
	dark, setDark := desktop.UseSetting("dark", false) // kept in the app's settings file
	return Div(Class("flex flex-col gap-4 p-6"),
		kit.Field{Orientation: kit.Horizontal, ControlAfter: true, Label: "Dark mode",
			Children: kit.Switch{Checked: &dark, OnCheckedChange: setDark.Set}},
		kit.Button{Children: Text("Done"), OnClick: win.Close})
}
```

**Desktop services** (`desktop`). Dialogs and notifications are asynchronous like a browser's: the call returns at once and the callback runs later **on the UI thread**, so it may set state. Call them from handlers and effects (from a goroutine, wrap the call in `tela.Post`; dev mode panics otherwise). Each returns an error when nothing was shown; it wraps `desktop.ErrUnsupported` when the desktop lacks the service (no XDG portal, no notification daemon, no tray host), and the app should fall back. In `tela snapshot` (no running app) they return an error.

- File dialogs: `desktop.OpenFile`, `OpenFiles`, `SaveFile`, `PickFolder(done, opts...)` with options `Title`, `Directory`, `DefaultName`, `Filter("Notes", "*.md", "*.txt")`, `Parent(win)`. `done(path, err)` gets `""` and a nil error when the user cancels. The dialog is modal to the window the call comes from.
- `desktop.ShowMessage(desktop.Message{Kind, Title, Text, Buttons, Parent}, func(desktop.Answer))`: kinds `MessageInfo/Warning/Error/Question`, buttons `ButtonsOK/OKCancel/YesNo/YesNoCancel`, answers `AnswerOK/Cancel/Yes/No`. Native on Windows; on Linux Tela draws it as a modal window. Escape or the close button answers Cancel (No for Yes/No).
- `desktop.Notify(desktop.Notification{Title, Body, Icon, Actions, OnClick, OnClose})` returns the shown notification (`Close()`). Windows shows no action buttons: keep every action reachable in the app. `Title` is required.
- `desktop.Tray{Icon, Tooltip, Menu, OnClick, OnError}` is a component: the icon is in the tray while it is mounted (`Icon` is one picture at several sizes, 16, 24 and 32 px; `Menu` is `[]desktop.MenuItem{Label, Separator, Checkbox, Checked, Disabled, Submenu, OnSelect}`; a checkbox item does not toggle itself). On GNOME without the AppIndicator extension `OnError` gets an `ErrUnsupported`: then do not hide the window on close.
- `desktop.UseSetting(key, def)` is `UseState` whose value lives in the app's JSON settings file (`desktop.Settings()` is the `*desktop.Store`: `Get`, `Set`, `Watch`). Values must encode as JSON; a stored value that no longer decodes reads as `def`.
- `desktop.PersistApp(app)` and `desktop.SavedWindow{Key, Window}` save and restore a window's size, maximized and fullscreen state and position. Wayland cannot place windows: only the size and state come back, and the position where the compositor restores sessions.
- Folders: `desktop.ConfigDir()`, `DataDir()`, `CacheDir()`, `StateDir()`, `LogDir()` (created on demand, named by `App.AppID` or `desktop.SetAppID("com.example.notes")`, called before the first read).

```go
package notes

import (
	"errors"
	"image"

	"github.com/kuronosu/tela"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/desktop"
	. "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
)

var trayIcon = []image.Image{image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, 32, 32))} // the app's icon at 16, 24 and 32 px (decode embedded PNGs)

// Editor opens a file, asks before closing and lives in the tray.
func Editor() tela.Component {
	return tela.C(func() tela.Node {
		win := tela.UseWindow()
		path, setPath := tela.UseState("")
		typing, setTyping := tela.UseState(false) // fallback: a field for the path
		open := func() {
			err := desktop.OpenFile(func(p string, err error) {
				if err == nil && p != "" { // "" is cancel
					setPath.Set(p)
				}
			}, desktop.Title("Open a note"), desktop.Filter("Notes", "*.md", "*.txt"))
			if errors.Is(err, desktop.ErrUnsupported) {
				setTyping.Set(true) // no portal in this session
			}
		}
		closeWindow := func() {
			desktop.ShowMessage(desktop.Message{
				Kind: desktop.MessageQuestion, Title: "Unsaved changes",
				Text: "Save the changes before closing?", Buttons: desktop.ButtonsYesNoCancel,
			}, func(a desktop.Answer) {
				if a != desktop.AnswerCancel {
					win.Hide() // the tray brings it back
				}
			})
		}
		return Div(
			desktop.Tray{
				Icon: trayIcon, Tooltip: "Notes", OnClick: win.Show,
				Menu: []desktop.MenuItem{
					{Label: "Show Notes", OnSelect: win.Show},
					{Separator: true},
					{Label: "Quit", OnSelect: tela.Quit},
				},
			},
			Button(OnClick(open), Text("Open…")),
			Button(OnClick(closeWindow), Text("Close")),
			If(typing, Input(Bind(path, setPath))),
			Text(path),
		)
	})
}
```

## 9. Pitfalls and limits

| Mistake | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Div("Hello")` does not compile | `Div(Text("Hello"))`; formatted: `Textf("%d", n)` |
| Calling a function component that uses hooks: `counter()`, `telatest.Mount(t, counter())`, `Card{}.Build()` (dev mode panics: "hook called outside its component") | `tela.C(counter)` (write a public `Counter()` that returns it once), `tela.CP(fn, props)`, or pass the struct value itself: `Card{}` / `Fragment(Card{})` |
| A hook inside `if`, a loop, a `Map`/`VirtualList` callback, an event handler, or after an early `return` | Call every hook at the top of the component; move per-row state into a row component (`MapKeyed(items, key, func(T) tela.Component { return Row{...} })`) |
| Returning a kit component (or `If(...)`) where a `tela.Node` is expected: `cannot use kit.Button{...} as tela.Node` | `Fragment(kit.Button{...})`, `Fragment(If(...))` |
| A list from `Map` without keys (dev warning "list without keys"), or index keys on a list that reorders | `Key(item.ID)` on each element; `tela.WithKey(comp, id)` for components; `MapKeyed` |
| Declaring a name that `h` exports in your package (`Button`, `Label`, `Input`, `Text`, `Icon`, `Form`, `Value`, `Name`, `Type`, `Key`, `Map`, `Range`, `Scale`, `Style`, `Rows`, `ID`, `P`, `A`, `Code`...): "already declared through dot-import" | Name it `SaveButton`, `FieldLabel`, `themes`... |
| `&Card{}` as a child, or a prop in a `tela.Component` field (`Children: Class("p-4")`): dev panic | Pass `Card{}`; put props in `Class`/`Props` |
| `setCount.Set(count + 1)` twice in one frame loses one | `setCount.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 })`; `tela.Toggle(setOpen)` for bools |
| `UseEffect(f, nil)` (dev panic) | `tela.UseEffect(f, tela.Once)` or `tela.UseMount(f)` |
| Unknown or misspelled class (`rounded-xxl`, `bg-primry`) | Dev error with "did you mean"; `tela lint ./...` finds them statically. Unsupported classes say what to use |
| A `kit.Tooltip` and a `kit.DropdownMenu` on the same `kit.Button`: a trigger takes one overlay | Tooltip on a wrapper: `kit.Tooltip{Content: Text("More"), Trigger: kit.TriggerFunc(func(p tela.Prop) tela.Node { return Span(p, Class("flex"), kit.DropdownMenu[string]{...}) })}` |
| A trigger that is not a `kit.Button` (an `h.Button`, an avatar) | `kit.TriggerFunc(func(p tela.Prop) tela.Node { return Button(p, ...) })`: put `p` on the element. `Disabled` goes on the overlay |
| `kit.Field` around `h.Input`, or around two controls: the label names nothing or the wrong one | One kit control per `Field` (`kit.Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, `DatePicker`, `ColorInput`); `RadioGroup`/`ToggleGroup` go in a `kit.FieldSet` (legend names them) or take `AriaLabel`; `Slider` and `Progress` take `AriaLabel` |
| An absolutely positioned icon over an input swallows clicks | `pointer-events-none` on the decoration: `Icon(lucide.Search, Class("pointer-events-none absolute top-2.5 left-3 size-4 text-muted-foreground"))` with `kit.Input{Class: "pl-9"}` |
| Scrolling to the newest item flickers or lands short | `UseLayoutEffect` + `ref.ScrollIntoView()` (or `ScrollToIndex(i, tela.AlignEnd)` on a `VirtualList`), deps = the item count |
| A flex child does not scroll or overflows | Give the scroll container a definite height (`h-screen`, `flex-1 min-h-0` in a `flex-col`, `h-96`) and `overflow-y-auto`; `min-w-0` on flex children that hold truncated text |
| Wanting `kit.Alert`, `kit.Sheet`, `kit.Accordion`, `kit.Breadcrumb`, `kit.Sidebar`, `kit.Combobox` | Not in kit: compose `Div`s with tokens (`Role("alert")` for an alert, a `Div` sidebar with `AriaCurrent`), or use `kit.Dialog`/`kit.Popover`; `aria` has `UseCombobox` for a hand-built one |
| `Variant: "primary"` on a `kit.Button` | The default variant is the zero value; variants are `Secondary`, `Outline`, `Ghost`, `Destructive`, `Link` |
| A kit page that looks off (square corners, wrong colors) | `Theme: &theme` with `theme := kit.Theme()` and `RootClass: "bg-background text-foreground"` on the `App` |
| Palette colors that ignore dark mode (`bg-white`, `text-zinc-900`) | Tokens (`bg-card`, `text-foreground`), or add `dark:` pairs |
| The snapshot does not show a toast or effect result | `tela snapshot` renders one frame; in `tela mcp`, act then `wait {"ms": 300}` and `screenshot` |
| `h.A` link does nothing | Tela does not navigate: handle `OnClick` |
| `Div(Class("flex"), children...)` with a `[]tela.Node` slice: Go cannot spread it | `Div(Class("flex"), Nodes(children))` |
| A `tela.Window` without `OnClose`: its close button does nothing | `OnClose: func() { setOpen.Set(false) }`: state owns whether a window exists |
| `desktop.OpenFile`, `ShowMessage` or `Notify` from a goroutine (dev panic), or state set in the callback of a goroutine | Call them from handlers and effects, or inside `tela.Post(func() { ... })`; their callbacks run on the UI thread |
| `App.OnClose` hides the window but nothing can show it again (no tray, or the tray is unsupported) | Pair it with a `desktop.Tray` whose `OnError` turns the hiding off; `tela.Quit` from the menu |
| `kit.TitleBar` in a window that keeps the OS's title bar: two bars | `Frameless: true`, or draw it only when `tela.UseWindow().State().ClientSideDecorations` |
| A test reads or writes the real settings and window placements | `telatest.TempDesktopDirs(t)` at its start |

**Limits.** Linux (Wayland, X11) and Windows windows; macOS cross-compiles but has no window yet. Wayland cannot place windows or keep them on top, and Windows notifications have no action buttons; a tray needs a host on Linux (GNOME needs an extension). No submenus in menus; `Checkbox` has no indeterminate state; `Select` has no search (build a combobox with `aria.UseCombobox`); `Table` has no virtualization, resizing or row selection UI; no date-time input; no `tela add` yet. No margin collapsing, floats or CSS tables; 2D transforms only; SVG icons have no text, filters or patterns; no `grid-template-areas` from classes; `vertical-align` only on inline-blocks.

## 10. Testing

`telatest` mounts a component in a headless window, drives it with real events, finds elements like Playwright and compares goldens (`testdata/<name>.png`; `TELA_UPDATE=1 go test ./...` writes them). Dev errors fail the test.

```go
func TestSettingsLike(t *testing.T) {
	app := telatest.MountFunc(t, func() tela.Node {
		on, setOn := tela.UseState(false)
		return Div(Class("p-6"),
			kit.Field{Orientation: kit.Horizontal, ControlAfter: true, Label: "Weekly digest",
				Children: kit.Switch{Checked: &on, OnCheckedChange: setOn.Set}},
			If(on, P(Text("Subscribed"))))
	}, telatest.Size(480, 200), telatest.Theme(kit.Theme()))

	digest := telatest.ByRole("switch", "Weekly digest")
	app.Expect(digest, telatest.Checked(false))
	app.Click(digest) // also: Fill(loc, text), Press("Shift+Tab"), Hover, Click(loc, telatest.Right()), Tap, LongPress
	app.Expect(digest, telatest.Checked(true), telatest.Disabled(false))
	app.ExpectText("Subscribed")
	app.Advance(500 * time.Millisecond) // the clock is manual: timers, UseTimeout, animations
	app.Golden("digest_on.png")         // telatest.Dark(), telatest.Scale(2) for other renders
}
```

`telatest.Mount(t, comp, opts...)` mounts any component (`Settings()`, `Page{}`, `Previews["x"]`); `telatest.MountApp(t, App, opts...)` mounts a `tela.App` as its window would. Locators: `ByRole(role, name)`, `ByText(text)`, `ByTestID(id)`, `ByClass(...)`, then `.Nth(i)`, `.Filter(telatest.HasText("x"))`. Expectations wait and retry: `Expect(loc, Checked/Pressed/Selected/Expanded/Disabled/Focused/Invalid(bool), Current("page"), HasName, HasValue)`, `ExpectText`, `ExpectNoText`, `ExpectRole`, `ExpectCount`, `ExpectValue`, `ExpectAria(yaml)`. `AriaSnapshot()`, `Screenshot()`, `Bounds(loc)`, `Resize(w, h)` inspect without waiting. Several windows: `app.Windows()`, `app.Window("Settings")` and `app.WaitForWindow(func() { app.Click(open) })` give an `*App` scoped to that window, with the whole API above; also `RequestClose()` (the close button), `Maximize()`, `Minimize()`, `ExpectWindowState(telatest.Maximized(true))` (`Fullscreen`, `Minimized`, `Hidden`, `Active`, `ClientDecorations`), `ExpectTitle`, `ExpectWindowCount(n)`, `ExpectClosed()`, `ExpectQuit()` and `ExpectRunning()` (an `OnClose` that hides the window). `MountApp` applies the window fields of the `tela.App` (`Frameless`, `OnClose`, size limits...); for a custom title bar, `HitRegions()`, `HitAt(x, y)` and `CaptionDrags()` show what the OS would do.

**Desktop services in tests.** The headless desktop shows nothing: it records dialogs, notifications and tray icons, and the test answers them, as the user would. Call `telatest.TempDesktopDirs(t)` first in a test whose app uses `desktop.UseSetting`, `PersistApp` or the app folders, or it reads and writes the real ones. Nothing answers by itself.

```go
package notes

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/desktop"
	"github.com/kuronosu/tela/telatest"
)

func TestEditorServices(t *testing.T) {
	telatest.TempDesktopDirs(t) // settings and window placements go to a temporary folder
	app := telatest.Mount(t, Editor())

	app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Open…"))
	app.AnswerFileDialog("/home/ana/ideas.md") // no paths: the user cancels
	app.ExpectText("/home/ana/ideas.md")

	app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Close"))
	app.AnswerMessage(desktop.AnswerYes) // native or drawn box: the same call
	app.ExpectWindowState(telatest.Hidden(true))
	app.ExpectRunning()

	app.ClickTrayItem("Show Notes") // also ClickTray(), Tray(), Trays()
	app.ExpectWindowState(telatest.Hidden(false))

	app.Unsupported(telatest.FileDialogs) // from now on OpenFile returns ErrUnsupported
	app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Open…"))
	app.ExpectRole("textbox", "") // the fallback path field
}
```

Also `app.Notifications()`, `ClickNotification(title)`, `ClickNotificationAction(title, label)`, `DismissNotification(title)` and `MessageBoxes()` / `FileDialogs()` to check what was asked. `Unsupported` takes `telatest.FileDialogs`, `MessageBoxes` (the box is drawn then), `Notifications`, `TrayIcons` and `OpenURLs`; with no arguments everything is supported again.
